subject: Call startup function prior to Shiny listening on port

messages.author: bef7f7aabe68e842
messages.subject: Call startup function prior to Shiny listening on port
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm new to Shiny, I have an app that loads quite a data frame from a database, then I display some plots / tables via Shiny. All is well when I load that state into my RStudio's global env manually, but when running standalone (from the command line), the UI fails because it tries to render before the data load finishes. However, the data load doesn't start until I attempt to load my app in the browser.

I'm looking for a startup hook. That is, way to run a function that runs once upon starting the shiny application, and freezes all other execution in the meantime. It'll take 30 seconds or so to load, then the server will start listening for requests. Is this possible? Note that running the function in the server.R file above the shinyServer() function doesn't do what I'm looking for.

Thank you,

Rob Sokolowski

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Call startup function prior to Shiny listening on port
parts:
Add a file called global.R in the same directory as ui.R and server.R. That should be exactly what you need, if you do the load there.

(If you are using Shiny Server Pro and encounter undesirable utilization_scheduler behavior with very slow global.R scripts, please contact sup...@rstudio.com; we have a fix for this problem that is not yet released but available for testing on request.)
